findings.what: Promotion cleanup deletes the attempt workspace before clearing the interrupted-promotion marker, so a real final-cleanup interruption can produce a manual-repair block that points to a workspace that no longer exists.
findings.why: `promote_workspace` writes the completed state, calls `discard_workspace(workspace)` at line 40, and only then unlinks `promotion.json` at line 41. A process stop between those calls—or any failure of the final unlink—leaves the marker that `recover_interrupted_promotion` treats as interruption evidence, but the retained workspace promised by AC4 has already been deleted. This does not ask for automatic rollback; it asks that the explicitly promised inspection workspace still exist whenever the marker triggers repair-required state. The new tests manually create the marker beside an intact workspace (`tests/test_pipeline_walk.py:648-649`) rather than reaching this producer ordering, so they cannot detect the defect. Add a deterministic public-behavior seam for the final cleanup boundary and change cleanup ordering so marker-triggered repair never references a deleted workspace.

They prove startup preserves an already-present workspace and ignores legacy backup/provenance fields, but never exercise the production cleanup sequence that can delete the workspace while leaving the marker.
